lessons.goal: 使用具體線索複習字義與避免重複錯誤。

questions.evidence: After a week of practice, the reading club reviews five words: purpose, damp, exchanged, exactly, and combination. Instead of copying each meaning five times, students write one short situation and underline the words that make the meaning clear to another reader.
questions.explanation: 底線畫在能釐清詞義的線索上。
options: Words that clarify the intended meaning.
Only the first word of each sentence.
The titles of all their textbooks.
Every word longer than five letters.

questions.evidence: Yun describes a towel that still feels a little wet. Her partner chooses damp. For exchanged, she writes about giving one ticket and receiving one book. A sentence about precisely eight meals helps the pair choose exactly rather than combination.
questions.explanation: 第二段用仍有些濕的毛巾說明。
options: A towel that is still a little wet.
A photo taken for a reason.
Eight meals counted precisely.
One ticket traded for a book.

questions.evidence: One ambiguous sentence is rewritten before the club keeps it in the review folder. The teacher explains that a useful practice question should contain enough clues for one best answer. Students leave with five situations they can explain, not only five translations they can repeat.
questions.explanation: 題目需足夠線索支持唯一最佳答案。
options: More than one choice could appear reasonable.
The folder has no room for long words.
Every sentence must contain a price.
The teacher wants students to stop explaining.
questions.prompt: Why does the club rewrite an ambiguous sentence?

questions.evidence: The combination card goes beside a description of rice boxes together with vegetable wraps. The last situation asks why a photo was taken, so its blank needs purpose. Each student checks whether a different card could fit just as well.
questions.explanation: 飯盒與捲餅放在一起形成組合。
options: A towel that has not dried.
A reason for taking a photo.
One meal counted precisely.
Different meal types put together.

options: A traded ticket—exactly; eight meals—exchanged.
